description: Inspect the source vacuum-tube amplitude-modulation apparatus: an AC transformer secondary is in series with the DC anode supply, and the oscilloscope is connected across the LC circuit. SOURCE FACTS: one circuit, four winding glyphs, capacitor, two unequal-plate cells, tube/filament, transformer core, two external audio terminals, two scope terminals and one screen trace. MODERN ADDITIONS: English component names and U_audio notation are declared on their text objects; original voltage suffix remains unresolved. Layout, regularized coil curves and the uncalibrated variable-height screen trace are not source measurements. No numeric voltage, frequency ratio, modulation depth, envelope curve, calibrated zero or endpoint is asserted as a source value. Author-only candidate, not a complete independent approval.

authoritativeText.text:
原书用电子管振荡器说明调幅：改变电子管两极（例如阳极与阴极）之间的电位差，可以调节其产生的高频电振荡的振幅。
在所述电路的适用工作范围内，该三极管的阳极与阴极间的电压增大时，阳极电流以及电源在一个周期内向振荡回路输送的能量通常随之增大，回路中的电振荡振幅也相应增大。
阳极电压降低时，输入回路的能量和振幅相应减小。

这是该电路的工作关系，不是任意电子管在任何工作状态下都成立的无条件规律。

当阳极电压变化的频率远低于振荡器产生的高频振荡频率时，在所述电路近似线性的工作范围内，振幅的变化可近似地与阳极和阴极间电压的变化成正比。
这里的正比关系是带有工作条件的近似，不是仅凭频率相差很大就能保证的精确关系。

在这个电子管电路示例中，为实现**调幅**，将附加的低频交流电源与直流阳极电源串联。
若变压器初级线圈中通有声频电流，次级线圈就可作为这个附加电源（图114）。
在上述工作条件下，振荡回路中高频振荡的振幅随阳极电压的变化而变化，从而使高频振荡按低频信号进行调幅。
将振荡回路的电压信号引入示波器，就可以在屏幕上观察被调制振荡随时间变化的波形。

The textbook uses a vacuum-tube oscillator to illustrate amplitude modulation: changing the potential difference between two tube electrodes, such as the anode and cathode, can adjust the amplitude of its high-frequency electrical oscillations. Within the operating range assumed for this circuit, an increase in the triode's anode-to-cathode voltage generally increases the anode current and the energy supplied by the power source to the oscillatory circuit during one period, with a corresponding increase in oscillation amplitude. When the anode voltage decreases, the energy supplied to the circuit and the amplitude decrease correspondingly. This describes the operation of this circuit, not an unconditional rule for every tube in every operating state.

When the anode voltage varies at a frequency much lower than the oscillator's high-frequency oscillation frequency, the amplitude change can be approximately proportional to the change in anode-to-cathode voltage within the approximately linear operating range of this circuit. This proportionality is a conditional approximation, not an exact relationship guaranteed solely by a large difference between the two frequencies.

In this vacuum-tube circuit example, **amplitude modulation** is produced by connecting an additional low-frequency alternating-voltage source in series with the direct-current anode supply. If an audio-frequency current flows through the primary winding of a transformer, its secondary winding can provide this additional source (Figure 114). Under the operating conditions described above, the amplitude of the high-frequency oscillations in the circuit varies with the anode voltage, so the high-frequency oscillations are amplitude-modulated by the low-frequency signal.
Feeding the voltage signal from the oscillatory circuit into an oscilloscope allows the waveform of the modulated oscillations to be observed as it changes with time.

inventory.description: Source: circular triode enclosure, upper plate, broken grid, separate curved cathode and filament with two descending unconnected heater leads. The anode, grid and cathode connect to the source circuit, not to invented power sources.

Source: two coupled upper windings; the right winding and two-plate capacitor share upper/lower buses; left winding connects grid to cathode return. Coil glyph curvature is regularized; lobes are not a measured turn count.

Source: lower transformer with two windings and a core; left winding is in series with the two-cell DC branch, right winding goes to two external terminals. Two DC cells retain short plate on the left and long plate on the right. There are no source printed + or - marks or voltage values.

Source: rectangular oscilloscope, one circular screen with one variable-height rapid trace, and two terminals connected across the LC buses. No source axes, calibrated zeros, endpoint values, or independent envelope exist.

Source: retain the electrical nets and visible bus junctions of the one connected apparatus. The lower transformer primary is electrically isolated from the series secondary; coupling is magnetic. The two heater leads remain unconnected as drawn.
